cards.text: This is a song of David, Israel's king, and he does NOT warm up. First line, he calls the LORD his light, his salvation and the stronghold of his life.

cards.question: With the LORD as his light, his salvation and his stronghold, what question does David ask?

cards.text: And David isn't talking theory. He remembers when the wicked came at him to devour his flesh, which, friend, is exactly how I go at a fresh tray of chocolate chip cookies, and it NEVER ends well for the cookies.

cards.question: When the wicked came at David, his enemies were the ones who stumbled and fell.

cards.text: Now David goes bigger. Not one enemy, a whole ARMY, camped all the way around him.

cards.question: Even if a war breaks out against him, David says he will keep his ___.
David says that with an army camped around him, his heart will be afraid.

cards.text: Then David says there's ONE thing he's asked of the LORD. Friend, if I only got one ask, I'd be pacing the bakery for six weeks with my mustache tied in knots.

cards.question: What's the one thing David asks of the LORD?

answers.text: To dwell in the LORD's house all his days
To see every one of his enemies defeated
To live a long and peaceful life in his land

cards.question: Living in the LORD's house, David wants to gaze on the ___ of the LORD and seek Him in His temple.

cards.text: David says a day of trouble WILL come. But he already knows what the LORD will do about it.

cards.question: In the day of trouble, what does David say the LORD will do for him?

answers.text: Send an army to fight for him
Bring down fire on his enemies

cards.question: After hiding David under the cover of His tent, where does the LORD set him?

cards.text: High upon a rock. Friend, I spent YEARS at the bottom of a junk drawer under the takeout menus, so that sounds like a penthouse to me.

cards.question: Set high on that rock, David says his head will be held high above his enemies around him.
With his head held high, what does David say he'll do at the LORD's tabernacle?

answers.text: Offer sacrifices with shouts of joy
Hang up his sword and his armor
Bow down in silence and weep

cards.text: Then David says, 'I will sing and make music to the LORD.' Six verses ago he had an army camped around him, and now he's warming up the CHOIR!
Then the song changes. David starts calling out: 'Hear, O LORD, my voice when I call; be merciful and answer me.'

cards.question: David says his own heart told him what to do. What did his heart say?

cards.text: And David answers his heart on the spot: 'Your face, O LORD, I will seek.' No 'let me check my calendar and circle back,' just YES.

cards.question: Now that he's seeking the LORD's face, David asks the LORD to hide His face from him.
As he pleads, David remembers what the LORD has already been to him. What does he say?

cards.text: So he asks the LORD not to leave him or forsake him. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer, and the only one checking on me was a dead battery who was NOT doing well himself.

cards.question: Though his father and mother forsake him, David says the LORD will ___ him.

cards.text: Then David asks the LORD to teach him His way and lead him on a level path. Friend, that's a man who has hit one too many potholes on the way to work.

cards.question: David asks for a level path because he's worn out from a long road.

cards.text: He begs the LORD not to hand him over to the will of his foes. And he names who's coming after him.

cards.question: Who does David say is rising up against him?

cards.text: And they're breathing out violence. Friend, I've opened a hot oven door that put out LESS heat than that.
Enemies. Lies. Violence. And then David says one little word that turns the whole song around: Still.

cards.question: Even with all that against him, David is certain he'll see the ___ of the LORD in the land of the living.

cards.text: David's got one last thing to say, and this time it isn't a request.

cards.question: What's the command David ends his song with?

answers.text: Lift your hands to the LORD
Go out and fight for the LORD

cards.question: Between his calls to wait for the LORD, David says be ___ and ___.

cards.text: Wait patiently for the LORD. Then he says it AGAIN. Friend, I bake for a living and I STILL open the oven door too early, so I'm pretty sure that line has my name on it.

findings.problem: The joke says devouring 'NEVER ends well for the cookies,' which casts the one being attacked as the loser. In Psalm 27:2 it is the attackers who stumble and fall. The joke points the baker toward the wrong pick on card 4.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it.

findings.problem: Psalm 27:3 is hypothetical ('Though an army encamps around me'). The card drops the 'though' and tells it as a real event: 'a whole ARMY, camped all the way around him.' 'All the way around' also stretches 'around me.'
The statement 'with an army camped around him' drops the 'though' of Psalm 27:3 and treats the army as already there.
'David says a day of trouble WILL come' stretches Psalm 27:5. The verse says what the LORD will do 'in the day of trouble.' It doesn't declare that trouble will come.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: 'After hiding David under the cover of His tent' puts the parallel lines of Psalm 27:5 in a time order. The text doesn't give one.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card only repeats 'High upon a rock,' which card 13 already answered, and adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: 'Six verses ago he had an army camped around him' is wrong. The army is in Psalm 27:3, three verses before 27:6. The line also treats the hypothetical 'though' army as real.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The card cites only Psalm 27:6 but also uses the army from Psalm 27:3.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: 'David answers his heart on the spot' adds an immediacy that Psalm 27:8 doesn't state.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The joke adds a new backstory fact: a dead battery as 'the only one checking on me' in the drawer. The backstory says the drawer friends were all in it together and that Papa Dorin was the one who checked on newcomers. Jokes may only invent small moments around his bakery.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The pothole joke suggests David wants a level path because of rough roads. That is the false statement on card 9. Psalm 27:11 says the reason is 'because of my oppressors.'

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it.

findings.problem: The card is a false statement, and no card ever tells the real reason David gives in Psalm 27:11: 'because of my oppressors.' The baker leaves without that detail.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The card cites only Psalm 27:13 but sums up 'Enemies. Lies. Violence.' from Psalm 27:11-12.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
